facts.statement: The genus Palaeotis was first described by Lambrecht in 1928.
The holotype of Palaeotis consists of a fossil tarsometatarsus and phalanx.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is a fossil tarsometatarsus and phalanx.

facts.statement: Houde and Haubold (1987) reclassified Palaeotis as a palaeognath in the order Struthioniformes, placing it with ostriches.
facts.quote: After a suggestion by Storrs L. Olson, a review of the type specimen and the referral of several other fossils by Houde and Haubold (1987) concluded that Palaeotis is a palaeognath and assigned it to the same order as ostriches; the Struthioniformes.

facts.statement: Houde and Haubold discovered three additional specimens of Palaeotis in the Geiseltalmuseum collection in Germany.
facts.quote: Houde and Haubold found three additional specimens in the collection of the Geiseltalmuseum, Martin-Luther University, Halle/S., Germany.

facts.statement: A specimen of Palaeotis cataloged as HLMD Me 7530 was collected from the Messel shales.
facts.quote: HLMD Me 7530 was collected from the famous Messel shales.

facts.statement: Palaeotis lived in central Europe during the middle Eocene epoch.
facts.quote: Palaeotis is a genus of paleognath birds from the middle Eocene epoch of central Europe.

facts.statement: The fossil record of Palaeotis spans from 48.07 to 41.03 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)

facts.statement: Palaeotis weigelti stood slightly under 1 meter tall.
facts.quote: P. weigelti was slightly under 1 meter tall.

facts.statement: Palaeotis possessed relatively large wings, indicated by its spindly humerus, unlike modern flightless birds.
facts.quote: While the forelimb is incomplete, the spindley humerus indicates that it had relatively large wings unlike modern ostriches and rheas.

facts.statement: Palaeotis likely had carnivorous habits, suggested by its slender beak similar to lithornithids.
facts.quote: The beak was slender, more similar to that of lithornithids, and probably had similar carnivorous habits.

facts.statement: Palaeotis is considered to be a flightless bird.
facts.quote: Paleotis is considered to be flightless.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Palaeotis was sexually dimorphic based on size differences between specimens.
facts.quote: Palaeotis is suggested to be sexually dimorphic, as some specimens being consistently smaller than others.

facts.statement: Some scientists debate the classification of Palaeotis, arguing it is a basal ratite rather than a struthioniform.
facts.quote: Other scientists are less convinced that Palaeotis is a struthioniform, placing it instead as a more basal ratite.

facts.statement: Some scientists are less convinced that Palaeotis is a struthioniform and instead place it as a more basal ratite.
facts.quote: Otro científicos están menos convencidos de que Palaeotis sea un estrutioniforme, situándolo en cambio como una ratites más basal.

facts.statement: Palaeotis weigelti is classified within the family Struthionidae.
The genus Palaeotis was established by Lambrecht in 1928.
The only known species of Palaeotis is P. weigelti.

rejected.statement: In 2021, Palaeotis was placed in the family Paleotididae alongside the genus Galligeranoides.
rejected.quote: In 2021, it was considered a member of the family Paleotididae alongside Galligeranoides from the Early Eocene of France.
